# TwoProd: an exact product as two limbs

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `two_prod` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $p + e$ of $a b$:

$$p + e \approx a b.$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet. It is part of [`mul_down_1`](mul_down_1.md), [`mul_up_1`](mul_up_1.md), [`mul_2_2`](mul_2_2.md), [`mul_2_1`](mul_2_1.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $p = \mathrm{RN}(a b)$.
- $\lvert p + e - a b\rvert \le \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$.
- $p + e = a b$ exactly, when $a b = 0$ or $\lvert a b\rvert \ge \eta/(2u^2)$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $2^{-1075} \approx 2.4703 \times 10^{-324}$ | $2^{-150} \approx 7.0065 \times 10^{-46}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0.0`, `0x1p-1074` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-149f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0.0`, `0x1p-1074` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-149f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `two_prod_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/EFT.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/EFT.v), against `two_prod_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions two_prod_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition two_prod_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  let '(p, e) := two_prod emin prec tie_even a b in
  fmt emin prec p /\
  fmt emin prec e /\
  p = RN emin prec (a * b) /\
  Rabs ((p + e) - (a * b)) <= (1 / 2) * eta emin /\
  (((a * b) = 0 \/ bpow radix2 (2 * prec - 1) * eta emin <= Rabs (a * b)) -> (p + e) = (a * b)).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `two_prod_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** TwoProd with an FMA (folklore; see [JMP17](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#jmp17)). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/two_prod.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/two_prod.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# TwoProd with an FMA. The rounded product is prod, an FMA with a zero addend, so that no compiler
# can contract it into the additions that consume it. Exact unless the product is tiny.

p = prod(a, b)
e = fms(a, b, p)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#two_prod)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound (always) | largest error / bound (when product large) | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 112 684 440 | 0 | 1 | 0 (exact) | yes |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 112 697 664 | 0 | 1 | 0 (exact) | yes |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 9 488 650 | 0 | 1 (`fp:7:-20:-6`) | 0 (exact) | yes |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
